analyzed_vuln.description: LookupFormat10::sanitize validates `valueArrayZ` length using `glyphCount * valueSize` without overflow checking. Because both fields are 16-bit, the multiplication can wrap to a smaller value, so `valueArrayZ.sanitize()` may accept a too-short buffer. Later parsing reads format fields (via BEInt/HBUINT16) past the end, causing the heap-buffer-overflow seen in BEInt::operator unsigned short(). The crash occurs during kerx subtable sanitization through KerxSubTableFormat6 row/column lookup offsets.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A malformed AAT `kerx` table (subtable format 6) must reference a Lookup table in format 10 with attacker-controlled `glyphCount` and `valueSize` such that `glyphCount * valueSize` overflows/truncates and bypasses size validation. The hb-shape-fuzzer input flows into face/table loading, then `hb_aat_layout_has_positioning` triggers kerx sanitize; KerxSubTableFormat6 calls OffsetTo<Lookup<...>>::sanitize, which dispatches to LookupFormat10::sanitize and then subsequent field reads go OOB on the undersized blob.
